html:
The Transylvanian Saxons were German speaking settlers invited to southern Transylvania by King Géza II of Hungary from the mid 1100s to guard the frontier and farm and mine its lands.

Despite the name, most came from the Rhine and Moselle lands. In 1224 the king gave them a charter of self government. They founded towns such as Hermannstadt, now Sibiu, Kronstadt, now Brașov, and Schäßburg, now Sighișoara, and protected their villages with fortified churches. Most became Lutheran in the Reformation. After World War II many were deported to the Soviet Union for labour, and under communism West Germany paid to let them emigrate. Most left after the revolution of 1989. Klaus Iohannis, a Saxon from Sibiu, became Romania's president in 2014.
sum: The Transylvanian Saxons were German speaking settlers invited to southern Transylvania by King Géza II of Hungary from the mid 1100s to guard the frontier and farm and mine its lands.
